title: Keeping a succulent alive, honestly
excerpt: Most of them die of kindness. How much light, how little water, and what to do when the leaves go soft.
content:
Most house plants that die are watered to death. A succulent stores its water in its leaves, and the kindest thing you can do is forget about it for a fortnight.

Three rules

  • The brightest sill you have
  • Water when the soil is dry all the way down, not before
  • A pot with a hole in the bottom, or very little water

When the leaves go soft

Soft, pale leaves mean too much water. Wrinkled leaves mean too little. Both can be put right if you notice within a week or two.

The echeveria in a concrete pot is a forgiving one to start with.
